facts.text: I have 1000 amps of fault current flowing through a rebar for 0.5 seconds.
I want to calculate the heat generated by a rebar (conductor) in concrete using the given fault current and time.
I searched online for an approximate resistance of the rebar in concrete for the purposes of my calculation.
I used the formula Q = I^2 * R * t with I = 1000 A, R = 2.53x10^-6 ohm, and t = 0.5 s.
I searched online for the specific heat capacity of concrete in joules per kilogram per degree Celsius.
The mass of concrete is 24000 kg.
I assumed the initial (summer) temperature of the concrete is 30 °C.

keyphrases: heat generated by rebar in concrete
heat rate Q = I^2 R t

events.text: Calculated heat generated Q using I^2 * R * t with I=1000 A, R=2.53x10^-6 ohm, t=0.5 s
Reported calculated heat amount Q as 1.265 J
Assumed initial concrete temperature as summer temperature 30 °C and planned to compute ΔT and final temperature
